Rama Ave. , Guadalupe 'Cebu City, Philippines Dear Mr. Lim: This is in response to your request for the Department's legal opinion on the effect of DILG Memorandum Circular 2015-143 on Cebu City Ordinance No. 2290. It appears that herein issue is centered to what you perceived as a seemingly conflicting provisions of Sec. 7a, lb, of Cebu City Ordinance No. 2290, and Section 3.2.5.2 (b) of DILG-DOH-DOF-DTI Joint Memorandum Circular (JMC) No. 1, Series of 2014 reiterated by DILG Memorandum Circular 2015-143 dated 2 December 2015. To provide a more comprehensive discussion on the matter, herein-below quoted successively are the provisions of the assailed regulations: sec. 7a. 1b, of Cebu City Ordinance No. 2290 "Section 7. Saföry Guidelines Strict compliance of [he following safety precautions, rules and regulations shall be observed by sellers und distributors of fireworks uncl pyrotechnic devices: u) The sale of fireworks and pyrotechnic device shall only be conducted by selleus distributors with business permit issued by the Cebu City Government in the follo wing areas and zones: 1) For Class I firevvolks and pyrotechnic devices: b) Shopping malls, provided that they are sold from sales booth and only in accordance wilh this Ordinance. For purposes of this Ordinance, shopping malls shul/ reför to a building or complex of buildings with shops that represent various merchandisers; and Sec.3.2.5.2 (b) of DILG-DOH-DOF-DTI loint Memorandum Circular (JMC) No. 1 Series of 2014

"Section 3.2.5.2 Display Center or "Firecracker and Pyrotechnic Zone (Section m4.65, IRR of'R.A. 9514) (b) Al! malls and other similar establishments shall not be utilized as display centers Ror selling OT firecrackers and pyrotechnics unless done through media presentation or other means without necessarily displaying the said firecrackers therein; 'The Departnnent opines that there is no conflict between the two assailed regulatory provisions. Basic is the rule [hat an ordinance that had gone through the legislative process eiijoys Lhe presumption of regularity. Considering that Cebu City Ordinance No. 2290 had through the substantive and procedural process for its passage and approval as Inanc121ed under the Local Government Code, it now enjoys the presumption of validity ancl should be presumed valid unless later judicially invalidated by a regular court. Be that as it may, what is evident is the insufficiency of Sec. 7a, lb of Cebu City Ordinance No. 2290 insofar as the allowable manner of selling firecrackers and pyrotechnic devices in shopping malls is concerned. On the other hand, Section 3.2.5.2 (b) of DILG-DOH„DOF-DTI Joint Memorandum Circular (JMC) No. 1 , Series of 2014, restrictively prescribed the specific safety requirement för the sale of firecrackers and pyrotechnics in shopping malls which is "only through media presentation or other means without displaying the said firecrackers therein". Having resolved that there is no conflict between the assailed regulations, the necessity to reconcile che same is hereby ruled out. Instead, it is respectfully enjoined that lhe regulatory intent contained therein be construed to supplement each other. We hope to have enlightened you on this matter. Ve truly yours, AUSTERE A.
